about: The format a Formula gives a General cell when it is entered (ADR-0047, second round). Microsoft does not document the rule for any function ExSheet declares (it does for DATE, TODAY and NOW, which ExSheet does not have), so the engine applies only what these cases have observed Excel to do: simple arithmetic (single-cell References, number constants, +, -, * and /, parentheses) takes the format of the first formatted cell it reads, except that a date minus a date gives none and a percentage is not carried through * or /; MIN, MAX and SUM over References and number constants take the format of their first formatted Reference; a number constant with % gives 0.0% only when added to or subtracted from an operand that gives no format, and otherwise none; anything else gives none. This is the smallest rule consistent with every observed case (ADR-0047, "What the third observation settled"). Multiplication, SUM and % were observed in the second run (verification/2026-09-27-windows-excel-2), division, SUM with a constant and % beside a formatted operand in the third (verification/2026-09-28-windows-excel-3), with real keys: through COM Excel formats fewer results, so those cases are asked by keys. It applies only when the cell's format is General, and only when the Formula is entered. The uncertain cases record the engine's answer where Excel has not been asked.

cases.description: A date plus a number shows as a date
A number plus a date shows as a date: the first formatted Reference, not the first operand
A date minus a date is a number of days, and gives no format
A Formula that is one Reference takes that cell's format
A negated Reference in parentheses takes that cell's format
The first Reference whose cell is formatted gives the format, an unformatted one before it passed over
A cell formatted before the Formula is entered keeps its format
The format is taken once, at entry: formatting the cell read afterwards does not change it
A cell read in a formatted column gives the column's format
A Formula pasted as text takes a format as a typed one does
Multiplication over a date takes the date format (verification/2026-09-27-windows-excel-2, with real keys)
